start_with: Inspect the job’s expected schedule and its most recent consecutive history rows.
Compare start time, stop time, status, status message, and duration rather than relying on the last status label alone.
Check whether the installed version predates the v19.5 fix for jobs silently stopping after errors while recording status, writing history, or sending notifications.
If rows are duplicated, falsely `Incomplete`, or show implausible durations for extremely fast work, check applicability of the separate v19.5 sub-second-history fix.
Verify the downstream result independently; history recording and business work are related but not identical outcomes.
Stop when version applicability or the installed job configuration cannot be established without live review. Rock release notes
branches.title: A scheduled job stopped producing new history
branches.when: A scheduled job stopped producing new history

start_with: On v19, capture the Page Load Time diagnostic and identify the slow component.
Compare an uncached or first request with a cached request.
If the expensive work is a large reusable dataset, inspect whether a Persisted Dataset is appropriate.
If the issue is intermittent or spans multiple pages, correlate it with infrastructure telemetry and exception timestamps.
Stop before enabling broad auditing or cache statistics unless their restart or performance effects are authorized. Approved claim source
branches.title: A page is slow

do_not_assume: Do not interpret an unchanged linked-key count as proof that the clear failed.
start_with: Identify whether the block uses Item Cache, Output Cache, Lava caching, or a Persisted Dataset.
Inspect the block’s assigned cache tags.
Clear only the relevant tag when one exists.
Do not interpret an unchanged linked-key count as proof that the clear failed.
If a Persisted Dataset supplies the data, inspect its producing job rather than repeatedly clearing output cache.
Verify the rendered page after the appropriate refresh path completes. Cache Manager Use Cache Tags
branches.title: Updated content remains stale

do_not_assume: Do not infer a filesystem-permission problem from this signature alone.
start_with: Record the exact exception and installed Rock version.
Check whether the error is `DirectoryNotFoundException` involving the cache directory.
Check applicability of the Rock v19.1 fix for the cache directory being removed by Rock Cleanup and not recreated.
Do not infer a filesystem-permission problem from this signature alone.
Stop if the signature or version differs; the pack supplies no broader cache-directory repair procedure.

branches.when: Clear Cache throws a missing-directory error

start_with: Open `Admin Tools > Settings > Exception List`.
Locate the grouped exception type and correlate its timestamps with the configuration change.
Open the exception detail and identify the affected page, block, or code path.
Revert or adjust only the configuration demonstrated to be involved.
Confirm whether the exception stops recurring.
If email alerts were absent, inspect the Exception List directly and separately verify the Email Exceptions List configuration.
branches.title: Exceptions repeat after a page or block change
branches.when: Exceptions repeat after a page or block change

start_with: Open the Universal Search Control Panel and confirm the provider connection error.
Inspect the configured provider under `Universal Search Index Components`.
Confirm that node URL, environment-specific credentials, and certificate fingerprint refer to the refreshed environment’s Elasticsearch service.
Verify the external service independently without exposing credentials.
Only after connectivity is restored, inspect entity indexing and re-index status.
branches.title: Universal Search cannot connect after an environment refresh
branches.when: Universal Search cannot connect after an environment refresh

start_with: Confirm that Person indexing is enabled.
Confirm that the specific attribute is selected for indexing.
Assess whether the attribute is safe to expose, because Universal Search does not enforce person-attribute security.
Run the supported Person bulk load or wait for the nightly re-index.
If the installed version predates v19.3, check applicability of the documented Person Attribute Values defect.
Stop if the desired attribute is sensitive or version applicability is unknown. Specifics for Entities
branches.title: A person attribute is missing from Universal Search
branches.when: A person attribute is missing from Universal Search

start_with: Confirm the provider is connected.
Confirm the entity is enabled in the Universal Search Control Panel.
Apply the entity-specific eligibility check: Group Type, Content Channel, site settings and crawl, calendar, or Person attribute.
Inspect the relevant re-index or site-crawl job history.
For sites, verify that the crawling starting location links to the missing content and that the crawler did not encounter an accessible logout link.
Re-index only after correcting eligibility or connectivity.
Verify one known eligible result after completion. Enable Entities for Universal Search
branches.title: An entity type returns no Universal Search results
branches.when: An entity type returns no Universal Search results

start_with: Confirm Universal Search is enabled in Search Services.
Confirm its position in the component list matches the intended default behavior.
Inspect the configured results URL and its Smart Search parameter.
Confirm the target page contains the Universal Search block.
Inspect which entities are allowed to appear through Smart Search.
Treat result templates and index contents as separate checks.
branches.title: Universal Search works directly but not through Smart Search
branches.when: Universal Search works directly but not through Smart Search

start_with: Open the candidate in Duplicate Finder.
Compare contact, name, family, birthday, Record Source, creator, modification time, and other available evidence.
Treat confidence as a heuristic.
If evidence is insufficient, defer the decision so Rock can reassess as records gain information.
Merge only when both records are established to represent the same person and the operator can review the values that will survive.
Stop when security restrictions or incomplete attribute visibility prevent a safe comparison. Use Duplicate Finder
branches.title: Two person records may be duplicates, but identity is uncertain
branches.when: Two person records may be duplicates, but identity is uncertain

start_with: Open `Tools > Data Integrity > Location Editor`.
Filter for locations that are not geocoded.
Open the affected location and correct its address fields.
Save so Rock can resolve coordinates again.
Verify the corrected location in the downstream feature that reported the problem.
branches.title: An address is missing coordinates

start_with: Identify which automation function changed the records.
Inspect its inclusion and exclusion Data Views, inactive-reason settings, and processing limit.
Check whether affected people were also changed in groups or security roles.
Correlate the changes with the Data Automation job’s execution history and audit information already available.
Do not rerun the job until the criteria and downstream effects are understood.
If temporary auditing is proposed, account for its significant performance cost. Use Data Automation

branches.when: Data Automation changed more records than expected
